findings.description: VO-8 previously distinguished a usage error (--review-file with --gate review, exit 2) from an INCONSISTENT verdict (exit 1). After the retarget both branches of the test assert exit 1, and the same @test already asserts exit 1 for a genuine inconsistency two lines above. The usage-error assertion can no longer fail if a regression routes the bad flag combination into ordinary verdict processing that happens to find the review file inconsistent.
findings.failure_mode: A future change that silently accepts --review-file on the review gate (and reports an INCONSISTENT verdict for unrelated reasons) passes VO-8 unchanged; the usage-error guard is no longer pinned by any assertion in this file.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the exit-1 assertion but also assert the usage-error marker the script emits (the round-1 notes say usage errors speak JSON with usage_error: true), e.g. [[ "$output" == *usage_error* ]] or a --json run checked with jq '.usage_error == true', so the two exit-1 paths remain distinguishable.

findings.description: NRM-20's comment claims the rc file is 'one file per repaired payload (its hops share it), never one per process', but the assertion is `sort -u rc-paths | grep -c . -ge 6`. The rc-paths file accumulates across the three rc_case iterations (2 payloads each, 5+5+6 hop calls), so a per-hop mktemp would yield 16 unique paths and also satisfy -ge 6. The only shape the assertion actually excludes is a single process-wide path, which the adjacent 'adv-repair-rc.' name check does not exclude either.
findings.failure_mode: A regression to one mktemp per hop (losing the shared-file semantics that lets a later hop read the earlier hop's exit code, or doubling temp-file churn) passes NRM-20 while the comment still asserts the opposite.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the count exactly: with three iterations of two payloads the unique-path count is 6 under the per-payload rule, so assert `[ "$(sort -u "$TEST_DIR/rc-paths" | grep -c .)" = "6" ]` (and optionally that each path appears at least twice, proving the hops of one payload share it).
